If \(n\le 93\), the 50 lightest and 44 heaviest overlap, but their union is all frogs. Since their total percentages sum only to \(57\%\), this is impossible.  
If \(n=94\), the two groups are disjoint but union to all frogs, again impossible because \(30\%+27\%\neq100\%\). Thus \(n>94\).

Then the 50 lightest and 44 heaviest are disjoint, leaving \(n-94\) middle frogs with \(43\%\) of the total mass. By ordering,
\[
\frac{0.30M}{50}\le \frac{0.43M}{n-94}\le \frac{0.27M}{44}.
\]
Cancel \(M\):
\[
0.006\le \frac{0.43}{n-94}\le \frac{0.27}{44}.
\]
So
\[
n-94\le \frac{0.43}{0.006}=71.666\ldots
\]
and
\[
n-94\ge \frac{0.43\cdot44}{0.27}=70.074\ldots
\]
Thus \(n-94=71\), so
\[
n=165.
\]

\boxed{165}
